targets.text: culture-rules transcribes a given audio file: an audio.transcribe action on an agent actor sends the file to an OpenAI-compatible speech-to-text endpoint (the lobes gateway), splits long audio, and a disabled transcribe-file bundle, fired by pocketsync.recording.landed, writes a timestamped transcript file and exports scalar outputs for whoever reads it next
the announcement ships whole: the action kind, the long-audio split, the disabled bundle and the result file all exist in the PR, and none of #73 items 4-9 do

audio.transcribe is a new action kind (culture_rules/model/action_kinds.py _k entry, a port in culture_rules/node/actions/, registered as action:audio.transcribe in node/runner.py default_ports) on an agent actor whose params mirror llm.complete: base_url, model, api_key grant:..., concurrency_pool, max_concurrency; validation reuses llm.py's _base_url_problem and grant resolve

audio.transcribe appears in ACTION_KINDS with typed params (actor, audio_path, audio_sha256, output_dir, language, model) and has a port registered under action:audio.transcribe, so test_default_ports passes

audio.transcribe reads its audio file only under an allowlisted root set in the actor's params and refuses a path outside it or a symlink that resolves outside it (error code path_refused); nothing in culture_rules does this today, so the containment code is new (the only precedent is io/gitrepo.py:56-60, resolve() + is_relative_to)

a path outside the root, a '..' escape and a symlink inside the root pointing outside it are all refused with path_refused before any byte is read or sent; the output_dir is held to its own allowlisted root the same way

the upload is a multipart POST to <base_url>/v1/audio/transcriptions with the fields file and language, built with the existing encode_multipart in node/actions/library.py:123-148 (stdlib only, no new runtime dependency)

the request is multipart with file and language fields to <base_url>/v1/audio/transcriptions with Authorization Bearer from the grant, no proxy, no redirects; the key never appears in errors or outputs

long audio (over 600 s or 16 MiB) is split by ffmpeg on the runner host into windows under both caps, cut at silences where ffmpeg silencedetect finds one, each window sent separately, and every segment's start/end offset by its window's start; ffmpeg/ffprobe are system binaries called through subprocess argv lists (no shell, the nosec B603 convention), present on spark at /usr/bin

windows are cut at detected silences when one falls in the search span and at the hard limit otherwise; window boundaries never overlap or drop audio, so the windows' durations sum to the file's duration within 0.1 s

the result file shape is {schema: 1, audio_sha256, model, language, duration, segments: [{start, end, text}], created_at}; while lobes returns only {text}, each window becomes one segment covering the window, and a later verbose_json response (lobes-cli#328) drops finer segments into the same list with no schema change
a plain {text} reply becomes exactly one segment {start: window start, end: window end, text}; a verbose_json reply with segments is offset and kept as-is; schema stays 1 in both cases

the action writes `<output_dir>/<audio_sha256>/transcript.<model-slug>.json` atomically (temp file then rename) under an allowlisted output root, and returns only scalars (result_path, result_sha256, audio_sha256, model, language, segment_count) so the transcript never sits in run state or in the rules.run.succeeded event
the result file is written to a temp file in the same directory and renamed, so a killed run leaves no partial transcript.*.json; the outputs carry result_sha256 of the bytes on disk

re-running the same (audio_sha256, model) is a cheap no-op: when the result file exists and its recorded audio_sha256 and model match, the action returns the existing file's outputs without calling the endpoint

the no-op check reads the existing file's audio_sha256 and model fields and also verifies the input audio's sha256 matches audio_sha256 before trusting either; a mismatch re-transcribes and replaces the file

failures end the run failed with distinct error codes: stt_unavailable (retryable: connection error, 5xx, 408, 429), stt_rejected (other 4xx incl. 413), audio_undecodable (ffmpeg/ffprobe or the endpoint's 400 invalid_audio), path_refused, plus the shared actor_kind_mismatch/secret_unresolved/stt_actor_invalid
each failure maps to exactly one code and only stt_unavailable is retryable; a run that fails ends in rules.run.failed with that code in error_code

a transcribe-file workflow (inputs audio_path, audio_sha256, language optional, model optional, output_dir; exported outputs result_path, result_sha256, audio_sha256, model, language, segment_count) ships in a bundle docs/rules/pocket-transcribe/ with actors/, workflows/, rules/ and variables like docs/rules/newspaper, the rule disabled, triggered by event type pocketsync.recording.landed with concurrency key stt:{trigger.data.audio_sha256}, and a bundle test like tests/rules/test_newspaper_bundle.py

the bundle imports cleanly into a MemoryStore with the rule disabled, passes the secrets scan, its workflow uses description and notes, and the rule's concurrency key is stt:{trigger.data.audio_sha256}

re-transcribe with a newer model is a direct workflows run transcribe-file --input model=... (cli/_commands/workflows.py:31-73, start_workflow typed inputs); since the file name carries the model slug, older results stay beside it
a direct run with model=X writes transcript.<slug(X)>.json and leaves an existing file for another model untouched

the new kind is wired everywhere the catalogue reaches: model/describe.py ACTION_WORDS, web/src/rules/ActionPicker.tsx (label/params table and an actorsFor case), web/src/api/types.ts kind union, tests/node/test_default_ports.py, an actor guide docs/actors/stt.md with a row in docs/actors/README.md; api/openapi.json has no action-kind enum, and CLI/MCP parity follows ACTION_KINDS with no extra registration
the editor's action picker offers audio.transcribe only with agent actors whose params carry base_url, and the web typecheck and vitest pass; docs/actors/stt.md exists with a README row
culture-rules never writes pocketsync-mongo or any recordings store, and never reads Pocket's transcript as input to its own; it reads the landed audio file and writes only its own result file
no new code opens a Mongo connection outside culture-rules' own store, and no step reads Pocket's transcript.json

pocketsync, which emits pocketsync.recording.landed and reads the result file back, and the operator, who enrols the STT actor, imports and enables the bundle; plus any later workflow that holds a path to an audio file
pocketsync can build its side from the committed docs alone: the event name and data fields, the workflow inputs, the result-file shape and the six outputs are written down in one place

only Pocket's own transcript exists; pocketsync's README (:26) lists re-running STT as a non-goal, no culture-rules action can send audio to the lobes STT route, and nothing in culture_rules reads a rule-supplied file path
on main b3a3025 there is no audio.transcribe kind and no code posting to /v1/audio/transcriptions

our own Hebrew-capable, timestamped transcript unblocks pocketsync own-transcription, and putting it in a generic file-in workflow keeps processing out of pocketsync, which shrinks to pull, webhook, events and its own store (#73)
transcribe-file has no input or step that names Pocket; only the bundled rule's trigger and input mapping do

with the bundle imported and its rule enabled, a pocketsync.recording.landed event makes a run on the STT actor's machine that writes `<output_dir>/<audio_sha256>/transcript.<model-slug>.json` and ends rules.run.succeeded with result_path, result_sha256, audio_sha256, model, language and segment_count in data.outputs; the same audio and model again is a no-op, and a different model writes a second file beside it
the after-state is proven by a test that drives a synthetic pocketsync.recording.landed event through the engine to a rules.run.succeeded event, not only by unit tests of the port

in tests with a fake STT server and synthetic audio: a 1500 s file is sent as at least 3 windows each <= 600 s and <= 16 MiB, every segment's start is offset by its window start within 0.05 s; a second run of the same (audio_sha256, model) makes 0 endpoint calls; 4 failure cases (endpoint down, undecodable audio, path outside the root, symlink escaping the root) end failed with 4 distinct error codes
the long-audio test really exceeds both caps' logic: the fake server refuses a window over 600 s or 16 MiB with 413, so an unsplit upload would fail the test
after rollout, one real recording longer than 600 s transcribes on spark through a direct workflows run transcribe-file with segment_count >= 2 and a Hebrew transcript the operator reads as usable
the live check uses a direct run on a file the operator picks; it does not need pocketsync to emit events first

windows are re-encoded to 16 kHz mono PCM16 WAV (32 000 bytes/s), so the 16 MiB upload cap binds at about 524 s before the 600 s cap does; windows are at most 480 s long, cut earlier at a silence when one falls in the last 60 s of the window
no window sent in the tests is longer than 480 s or larger than 16 MiB, including the last one

a retry resumes rather than restarts: each window's reply is kept in a work directory under the output root keyed by (audio_sha256, model), a retried attempt sends only the windows still missing, and the work directory is removed after the final rename
a test fails one window mid-file with a retryable error and the retry sends only that window and the ones after it

the bundle's transcribe step sets timeout_s 14400 explicitly, because the engine default DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S is 3600 s (engine/runs.py:306) and the longest landed recording is 3.8 h; with resume, a timed-out attempt continues on retry
the bundle test reads the transcribe step's timeout_s and asserts it is at least 14400

audio_sha256 must be 64 lowercase hex characters (invalid_request otherwise) before it forms any path, and the action hashes the audio file and refuses a mismatch with audio_mismatch before transcribing, not only on the no-op path
a crafted audio_sha256 such as '../../etc' never reaches a filesystem call, and a file whose hash differs from the event's is never sent to the endpoint

silent gaps stay visible: a window whose reply text is empty is kept as a segment with empty text, and the result file carries window_count and empty_window_count, because lobes drops low-confidence 30 s chunks (MIN_AVG_LOGPROB) without saying so until lobes-cli#328's dropped[] ships
a fake reply of empty text for one window yields a segment with text '' at that window's times and empty_window_count 1
a missing ffmpeg or ffprobe on the actor's machine fails at once with ffmpeg_missing (not retryable), naming the binary, instead of a generic error
a test with ffmpeg absent from PATH ends failed with ffmpeg_missing and no endpoint call

tasks.summary: Audio split module: ffprobe duration, silence-aware windows of at most 480 s, WAV window extraction
acceptance_criteria: plan_windows(1500, silences) returns contiguous non-overlapping windows covering 0..1500 within 0.1 s, none longer than 480 s, cut at a silence inside the last 60 s of a window when one exists, else at 480 s
a 480 s window extracted as 16 kHz mono PCM16 WAV is under 16 MiB (asserted on the real file)
require_tools() with a PATH lacking ffmpeg raises naming ffmpeg; tests skip cleanly when ffmpeg is not installed
tasks.instruction: New stdlib module culture_rules/node/actions/audio_split.py, tests in tests/node/test_audio_split.py. Functions: require_tools() -> raises a ToolMissing naming ffmpeg or ffprobe (shutil.which); probe_duration(path) via ffprobe; plan_windows(duration, silences, max_s=480, search_s=60) pure function returning [(start, end)]; detect_silences(path) via ffmpeg silencedetect parsing stderr; extract_window(path, start, end, dest) writing 16 kHz mono PCM16 WAV. subprocess argv lists only, timeouts, '# nosec B603'. Tests generate audio with ffmpeg (sine + silence gaps, lavfi) in tmp_path and skip with a reason when ffmpeg is absent; plan_windows is tested without ffmpeg. Never commit audio.

tasks.summary: Transcript result file: schema-1 builder, model slug, atomic write, existing-result read, per-window work dir
acceptance_criteria: build_result with one plain-text window at 480-960 s yields one segment {start 480, end 960}; a segments reply at window start 480 shifts each segment by 480; an empty reply yields a '' segment and empty_window_count 1
write_atomic leaves no partial transcript file when the write raises midway (temp file removed), and returns the sha256 of the file on disk
WorkDir put/get round-trips per window, survives a new WorkDir instance (resume), and clear() removes it
tasks.instruction: New stdlib module culture_rules/node/actions/transcript_file.py, tests in tests/node/test_transcript_file.py. model_slug(model) replaces every char outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] with '-'. result_path(output_dir, audio_sha256, model). build_result(audio_sha256, model, language, duration, windows) where windows is a list of (start, end, reply) and a reply is {text} or {text, segments[]}: plain text -> one segment spanning the window, segments offset by window start, empty text kept as '' segment; adds window_count, empty_window_count, schema 1, created_at. write_atomic(path, doc) via NamedTemporaryFile(dir=same dir) + os.replace, returns sha256 of the bytes written. read_existing(path) returns the doc or None. WorkDir(output_dir, audio_sha256, model): get(i)/put(i, reply) atomic per-window JSON, clear() removes the dir.

acceptance_criteria: a generated 1500 s file is sent as >= 4 windows each <= 480 s and <= 16 MiB, and every segment start equals its window start within 0.05 s; an unsplit upload would get 413 from the fake
a second run with the same audio and model makes 0 transport calls and returns the same outputs

path outside audio_root, a symlink escaping it, an output_dir outside output_root -> path_refused; a bad audio_sha256 -> invalid_request; changed bytes -> audio_mismatch; ffmpeg missing -> ffmpeg_missing; garbage audio -> audio_undecodable; 400 from the endpoint -> stt_rejected; connection refused -> stt_unavailable; none of them calls the endpoint except the last two

tasks.instruction: New culture_rules/node/actions/stt.py modelled on node/actions/llm.py (LlmCompletePort): check_stt_actor (agent kind, base_url via llm._base_url_problem, model, grant api_key, audio_root, output_root), _Refused `<code>: <detail>` errors, ReplayLedger, injectable transport reusing library.encode_multipart and a no-proxy no-redirect urllib opener; per-request timeout min(remaining deadline, 900 s). Order: validate audio_sha256 regex -> roots (resolve strict, is_relative_to) -> require_tools -> stream-hash the audio (audio_mismatch) -> existing result no-op -> probe/plan/extract windows into a TemporaryDirectory -> for each window not in WorkDir: POST, parse, WorkDir.put -> build_result, write_atomic, WorkDir.clear -> completed outputs. Register 'action:audio.transcribe' in node/runner.py default_ports and update its docstring (the catalogue entry lands in t3, after this task; a port with no catalogue entry is harmless). tests/node/test_audio_transcribe.py calls the port directly with a fake transport that answers 413 for a body over 16 MiB or a WAV over 600 s.
